variables.content:
A two-site (double quantum-dot) model where each quantum dot represents the localized state at one sulfur atom, coupled to electrode continua and to each other, reproduces the principal transmission features when parametrized by interdot tunneling $t_{c}$ and electrode–dot couplings $\gamma_{1}$ and $\gamma_{2}$. The model transmission used is
      $$
      T(E)=\frac{4\bigl[t_{c}\bar{\gamma}-\gamma_{12}(E-\bar{E})\bigr]^{2}}{\bigl[(E-\bar{E})^{2}-\bigl(\tfrac{\Delta E}{2}\bigr)^{2}-t_{c}^{2}-\bigl(\tfrac{\Delta\gamma}{2}\bigr)^{2}\bigr]^{2}+4\bigl[\bar{\gamma}(E-\bar{E})-t_{c}\gamma_{12}\bigr]^{2}},
      $$
      with $\bar{E}=(E_{1}+E_{2})/2$, $\Delta E=E_{1}-E_{2}$, $\bar{\gamma}=(\gamma_{1}+\gamma_{2})/2$, $\Delta\gamma=\gamma_{1}-\gamma_{2}$, and $\gamma_{12}=(\gamma_{1}\gamma_{2})^{1/2}$. Fitting the first-principles $T(E)$ with this expression captures the two main peaks and their asymmetries, thereby justifying the DQD interpretation of the junction as two localized contact states (MIGS/BEIS) coupled through the alkane bridge and to electrode continua.
variables.title: Double quantum-dot model and analytical transmission formula fit first-principles T(E)

variables.content: AD-NEGF enables gradient-based inverse optimization of Hamiltonian matrix elements to fit a target transmission curve. In an example, starting from the Hamiltonian $H_{52}$ of a 5-2 graphene nano-junction (consisting of 5 graphene rings on the left and 2 on the right) as the initial guess, gradient-based minibatch optimization over 2000 energy-sampled transmission $T(E)$ points and roughly $10^{4}$ Hamiltonian parameters (including device, leads, and couplings) was performed with the Adam optimizer; the loss decreased substantially within a few hundred iterations and the optimized $H_{52}$ produced a transmission curve qualitatively approximating the target transmission $T_{74}(E)$ of a 7-4 graphene nano-junction (7 rings left, 4 rings right). Conventional black-box optimizers (Bayesian optimization, genetic algorithms, and finite-difference gradient methods) failed on this high-dimensional fitting task due to the curse of dimensionality.
variables.title: Gradient-based inverse design of Hamiltonian to fit target transmission (transmission-by-design)

variables.content: The stationary tunneling probability spectrum of a single electron through a GaAs/InAs double quantum dot shows that a single resonant-transmission peak associated with an isolated dot splits into two distinct resonance peaks when the two dots are coupled; the energy separation between the two split resonance peaks increases as the interdot distance $d$ decreases (stronger interdot coupling), and the splitting becomes negligible when $d$ is sufficiently large (example parameter set: $R_1=R_2=5.0\ \mathrm{nm}$, $L_1=L_2=4.0\ \mathrm{nm}$; results displayed for $d=0,\ 1.0,\ 2.0,\ 4.0,\ 8.0\ \mathrm{nm}$).
variables.title: Resonance-energy splitting increases with stronger interdot coupling

variables.content: In the 2QD-T system (double quantum dot T-shaped) with symmetric dot–lead coupling ($\Gamma_L=\Gamma_R=\Gamma$) and equal dot levels ($\epsilon_1=\epsilon_2=\epsilon$), for strong inter-dot coupling ($t_{12}\gg\Gamma$) the transmission evolves with a single dominant relaxation time $\tau^{osc}=2/\Gamma$ from an initial single-peak (corresponding to transmission through the single quantum dot) into a stationary double-peak spectrum corresponding to bonding and anti-bonding resonances at $E_{\pm}=\epsilon\mp\Delta/2$ (width $\Gamma/2$), where $\Delta=\sqrt{4t_{12}^{2}-\Gamma^{2}}$ is the bonding–antibonding splitting. During this evolution pronounced dot–electrode charge oscillations occur; these oscillations can make the time-dependent transmission change sign at certain energies and thus can transiently reverse the direction of the current flow.
variables.title: Strong-coupling physical outcome: single relaxation time evolution into bonding/antibonding resonances and transient current reversals

variables.content: For the non-interacting double-dot dynamics and steady-state quantities (current, mutual information, concurrence), results obtained from (i) exact unitary time evolution of a large discretized bath (128 levels per lead) and (ii) the steady-state NEGF/EOM formalism agree quantitatively across the parameter regimes explored, with small discrepancies attributable to finite discretization of the bath spectrum in the exact numerics.
variables.title: Validation: exact numerics and NEGF (EOM) agree in the non-interacting limit

variables.content: Transport calculations based on a master-equation approach using a double quantum dot model with one spin-degenerate orbital per dot, with parameters extracted from the experiment (including interdot tunnel coupling t = 0.14 meV, spin-orbit parameter α = 0.6, effective g-factor |g| = 8.9, charging energies, and lead couplings), fully reproduce the measured transport spectrum for the one- to two-electron transition in a parallel InAs nanowire double quantum dot (cooldown B) as a function of level detuning and magnetic field, including the conductance map at B = 2 T and V_SD = 2.5 mV.
variables.title: Master-equation transport calculation with one orbital per dot reproduces one-to-two electron transition spectrum

variables.content: A parameterized tight-binding model consisting of a linear chain of single-orbital sites representing the dangling-bond wire (DBW) coupled to identical one-orbital dangling-bond centers (DBCs) was fitted to the first-principles results obtained from nonequilibrium Green's function density functional theory (NEGF-DFT) and reproduces the principal features of the NEGF-DFT transmission spectra: a transmission dip produced by a single DBC, the suppression of the second propagating channel, and the splitting of density of states (DOS) and transmission dips for closely spaced coupled DBCs. The model thereby provides a simple physical picture of a continuum wire coupled to localized dot states that captures the qualitative gating mechanism observed in the ab initio calculations.
variables.title: A minimal tight-binding model reproduces main NEGF-DFT gated DBW transport features

variables.content: When DeepQTH equilibrium Hamiltonians and DeepQTV-derived Hamiltonian corrections are combined and provided to the quantum transport solver TBtrans, DeepQT yields transport observables matching full Non-Equilibrium Green's Function combined with Density Functional Theory (NEGF-DFT) references for challenging, large-scale devices: (a) nanoporous graphene nanoribbon device (422 atoms, circular pore diameter 8 Å) — predicted wave-vector-averaged transmission spectrum across $[-1.5, +1.5]$ eV, electrode spectral densities, atom-resolved density of states (DOS) spatial decay from pore edge, and current–voltage (I–V) curve match NEGF-DFT references with low error; (b) heavily doped silicon Esaki (tunnel) diode (384 atoms, doping $\sim 8\times10^{20}\ \mathrm{cm}^{-3}$) — DeepQT-predicted Hamiltonians across biases $-1.0$ to $+1.0\,$V reproduce the nonlinear I–V and capture the negative differential resistance (NDR) region between 0.2 and 0.5 V, consistent with reference self-consistent calculations using TranSIESTA and the TBtrans solver.
variables.title: Accurate transport predictions on large, defected devices including nanoporous graphene and Esaki diode

variables.content: When trained on density functional theory (DFT) electronic-structure labels computed with the ABACUS package, the deep learning tight-binding (DeePTB) model reproduces the conduction and valence band dispersions of monolayer MoS$_{2}$ near the K and $\Gamma$ points in the Brillouin zone and captures the magnitude of the direct band gap; the combined DeePTB and non-equilibrium Green's function (DeePTB-NEGF) pipeline then produces a transmission spectrum computed over the energy range from -10 eV to 10 eV with a 0.05 eV step that reflects semiconducting behavior (negligible transmission within the gap and gradual emergence of conducting channels at higher energies). Because ABACUS does not provide a native NEGF reference calculation, the transmission spectrum is derived from the DeePTB-fitted Hamiltonian without direct DFT-NEGF benchmarking.
variables.title: Reproduction of monolayer MoS$_2$ band structure from DeePTB model trained on ABACUS DFT data and DeePTB-NEGF transport prediction without DFT-NEGF benchmark

variables.content: The analytic Green‑function expressions, the Landauer‑type current formula, and the derived relations for occupancies and static susceptibility constitute a framework that, within the noninteracting double quantum dot model (i.e., no electron–electron interactions) and, for the multilevel case, under the approximation of energy‑independent hopping integrals, applies at arbitrary temperature, arbitrary dot–lead and interdot coupling strengths, and arbitrary bias and gate voltages. The framework formally extends to nonlinear response, asymmetric couplings, and finite‑bias/finite‑temperature gradients within the same nonequilibrium Green function (NEGF) formalism used here.
variables.title: Scope: framework applies at arbitrary temperature, couplings, and biases; extensible to nonlinear and asymmetric cases

variables.content: Tight-binding and material-specific DFT-NEGF calculations for two meta-connected OPE3-type molecules M2 and M3, each containing a single pyridinic nitrogen atom at different positions, show that increasing the on-site energy of the pyridinic nitrogen site ($\varepsilon_p$), which models protonation or methylation, causes an interchange of frontier orbital ordering that changes the quantum interference (QI) pattern: in M2 the highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) and HOMO-1 interchange and in M3 the lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) and LUMO+1 interchange, and these reorderings convert a low-transmission destructive-QI anti-resonance into a high-transmission constructive-QI spectrum near the electrode Fermi energy. This mechanism is captured both in simple tight-binding parameter sweeps of $\varepsilon_p$ and in material-specific transmission spectra.
variables.title: Increase in on-site energy of the pyridinic nitrogen site interchanges frontier orbital ordering and switches quantum interference from destructive to constructive in M2 and M3

variables.content: In a single-electron two-dimensional rectangular quantum dot model (width $W_{\mathrm{QD}}$, length $L$, leads of width $W$) treated with an $S$-matrix scattering formalism using transverse-mode expansions $\Psi_{L}(x,y)$ and $\Psi_{\mathrm{QD}}(x,y)$ and channel momenta $k_{n}^{L,R}=\sqrt{2m^{*}E/\hbar^{2}-(n\pi/W)^{2}}$, $q_{m}=\sqrt{2m^{*}E/\hbar^{2}-(m\pi/W_{\mathrm{QD}})^{2}}$ with effective mass $m^{*}=0.067$ a.u., the computed transmission spectrum (single open left and right channel energy range) exhibits a reversal of the Fano asymmetry parameter $q$ at energy approximately $E\approx 42\ \mathrm{meV}$. At this energy the transmission goes nearly to zero at a shape-resonance position, indicating strong destructive interference produced by coupling between an open-channel shape resonance and closed-channel Feshbach resonances. The transmission $T_{n}$ is computed from the $S$-matrix via $T_{n}=\sum_{m}\dfrac{k_{m}^{R}+k_{m}^{R^{*}}}{k_{n}^{L}+k_{n}^{L^{*}}}\left[\mathrm{S}_{21}\right]_{m,n}\left[\mathrm{S}_{21}^{*}\right]_{m,n}$.
variables.title: Numerical demonstration of q reversal in a rectangular 2D quantum dot model at E ≈ 42 meV

variables.content: Synthesizing the controlled local density of states (LDOS) measurements and non-equilibrium Green's function density functional theory (NEGF-DFT) transmission results, the study identifies single-row dimer wires as "good" candidates and wider dimerized wires (e.g., double-dimer wires) as "best" candidates for atom-scale transport and quantum-dot applications because they (i) possess multiple discrete mid-gap states arising from $\pi$-type hybridization that extend well into the apparent bandgap (reducing leakage to bulk), (ii) show higher low-bias transmission (e.g., measured/modelled $T\approx 0.7$ for single-dimer and $T\approx 1.3$–$1.5$ for double-dimer geometries), and (iii) exhibit enhanced resilience to localized hydrogen defects and mechanical buckling compared to single-atom-wide or zig-zag geometries.
variables.title: Identification of dimer and wider dimer wires as practical candidates for atom-scale transport and quantum-dot applications

variables.content: For a 2‑quantum‑well MgO/NM superlattice in which each ARR termination consists of a quantum well identical to the superlattice wells and a barrier whose width is half that of the superlattice barriers, coherent non‑equilibrium Green's function (NEGF) quantum transport calculations for a representative transverse mode with transverse mode energy E_{t}=0.1 eV show that the transmission spectrum of the structure is modified from a set of narrow resonant transmission peaks (the resonances of the bare superlattice) into a broadened continuous band‑pass transmission window within the miniband; in other words, the ARR design acts as an electronic analog of an optical anti‑reflection coating and produces a broadened band of high electronic transmission instead of isolated narrow resonances.
variables.title: Anti‑reflective terminations broaden superlattice resonances into a band‑pass window

variables.content: Nonequilibrium Green's-function (NEGF) quantum-transport calculations for a model two-terminal device geometry predict that, at energies close to the Fermi energy E_F, the number of conducting transmission eigenchannels is zero for majority-spin carriers and two to three for minority-spin carriers, so that the computed quantum transmission corresponds to an electrical conductance that is fully spin polarized (100% spin polarization) near E_F; this transmission spectrum therefore implies that the polymer, in the coherent ballistic transport regime assumed by the calculations, can act as a perfect spin filter.
variables.title: NEGF quantum-transport prediction of fully spin-polarized conductance near the Fermi level
